key_insight: Partially fault-tolerant encoding with the [[4,2,2]] Iceberg code can improve noisy quantum simulation accuracy without requiring a fully fault-tolerant gate set.
engineering_relevance: This shows a practical path to better near-term quantum simulation on IBM superconducting hardware by trading modest encoding overhead for stronger error suppression and lower circuit depth.
method: Encode 42 logical qubits using 21 Iceberg-code blocks on IBM ibm_boston.
Combine fault-tolerant syndrome extraction with non-fault-tolerant logical operations.
Use Observable-Ranked Postselection to filter results based on syndrome correlations while limiting shot loss.
evidence_signal: Across Ising-model simulations in 1+1D and 2+1D, the encoded approach outperformed the unencoded baseline for local observables, with gains of 2–6% at intermediate times and over 200% at the latest 2+1D times studied.
watch_item: The approach still depends on noisy hardware, and selective postselection can reduce usable data if syndrome correlations are not well matched to the device behavior.
paper_title: Realizing Error Suppression in Partially Fault-Tolerant Quantum Simulations with IBM Quantum Computers
